diagnostics.title: Invalid rule parameter
diagnostics.summary: A rule attribute received a literal that cannot be converted to the member's type. The generator stops before it emits a rule that would fail at runtime.
diagnostics.message: error VAL0001: The value "true" cannot be parsed as type "Boolean" for rule "Equal"
diagnostics.fix: Converts the literal to the expected type; for a Boolean it removes the quotes.
diagnostics.guidance: Use the literal form of the member type. The converter covers Boolean, DateOnly, DateTime, Decimal, Enum, Guid, and TimeSpan literals; it does not guess a value that the source does not contain.

diagnostics.title: Rule applied to incompatible property type
diagnostics.summary: The attribute describes a check that the member's type cannot support. The generator refuses to emit an impossible rule.
diagnostics.message: error VAL0002: Rule "Email" cannot be applied to property "Id" of type "int"
diagnostics.reason: Changing the rule or changing the member type are both valid designs. An automatic fix would have to guess which one the author intended.
diagnostics.guidance: Use a string member for [Email], or choose a rule that matches the numeric member (for example [GreaterThan]).

diagnostics.title: Rule parameter type mismatch
diagnostics.summary: The rule parameter has a different type from the value it must compare. The generator cannot choose between converting the parameter and changing the rule.
diagnostics.message: error VAL0003: Rule "InclusiveBetween" expects a parameter of type "Int32", but received "String"
diagnostics.reason: The literal or the rule may be wrong; the intended change is ambiguous and no safe automatic rewrite exists.
diagnostics.guidance: Pass numeric literals for numeric members: [InclusiveBetween(18, 99)]. Use the literal type that matches the member, not a string that happens to look numeric.

diagnostics.title: Nested validator not found
diagnostics.summary: A [Nested] property points at a type that has no generated validator, so the nested rules would silently never run.
diagnostics.message: warning VAL0004: No validator was found for nested type "Address"
diagnostics.reason: The missing nested validator must be authored; the generator cannot invent the rules for another model.
diagnostics.guidance: Annotate the nested type with [Validate], or register a validator and reference it explicitly. A type without [Validate] has no generated validator to call.

diagnostics.title: Collection element validator not found
diagnostics.summary: A [ForEach] collection points at an element type that has no generated validator, so the elements would not be validated.
diagnostics.message: warning VAL0005: No validator was found for collection element type "LineItem"
diagnostics.reason: The missing element validator must be authored; the generator cannot infer the element rules from the collection declaration.
diagnostics.guidance: Annotate LineItem with [Validate], or use an explicit child validator through the fluent API.

diagnostics.title: Rule cannot be used on nullable type
diagnostics.summary: A numeric or comparison rule is applied to a nullable member. If null should be rejected, the declaration needs [NotNull] before the rule.
diagnostics.message: warning VAL0006: Rule "GreaterThan" cannot be applied to nullable type "int?" on the property "Quantity". Consider adjusting the rule "GreaterThan" or using a non-nullable type.
diagnostics.fix: Adds [NotNull] before the numeric rule so the generated validator rejects null explicitly.
diagnostics.guidance: Keep the nullable member when null has meaning, but make the intent explicit: [NotNull] rejects null, while a non-nullable member makes null impossible by type.

diagnostics.title: Conflicting rules on property
diagnostics.summary: Two bounds describe an impossible range, such as a value that must be greater than 100 and less than 50.
diagnostics.message: error VAL0007: Property "Age" has multiple conflicting rules: GreaterThan(100) and LessThan(50) create an impossible range.
diagnostics.fix: Removes one of the conflicting rules, leaving the author's remaining bound.
diagnostics.guidance: Choose the bound that expresses the real requirement. If the property truly needs a range, use [InclusiveBetween] or [ExclusiveBetween] with the intended lower and upper bounds.

diagnostics.title: Unsupported attribute argument type
diagnostics.summary: An attribute argument has a CLR type that the rule cannot turn into a validation parameter.
diagnostics.message: error VAL0008: Attribute argument "typeof(string)" is not supported for rule "Equal"
diagnostics.reason: The supported argument contract depends on the rule's intended shape; the generator cannot choose a conversion that preserves the author's intent.
diagnostics.guidance: Use a primitive, string, enum, or other rule-supported constant. If the value is genuinely a type, model that requirement with a custom rule.

diagnostics.title: Invalid rule combination
diagnostics.summary: Two rules imply incompatible minimum lengths. [NotEmpty] requires at least one character while [Length(0, …)] permits the empty string.
trigger: public string Name { get; set; } = string.Empty;
diagnostics.message: error VAL0009: Rule "NotEmpty" cannot be combined with rule "Length" on the same property "Name"
diagnostics.fix: Raises the Length minimum to 1, or removes [NotEmpty] when the length rule is sufficient.
after: public string Name { get; set; } = string.Empty;
diagnostics.guidance: Keep one statement of the minimum length. [Length(1, 100)] already expresses the non-empty requirement.

diagnostics.title: Rule parameter out of range
diagnostics.summary: A range rule has its lower bound above its upper bound, so no value can satisfy it.
diagnostics.message: error VAL0010: Parameter "10" for rule "InclusiveBetween" is outside the valid range for type "Int32"
diagnostics.guidance: Write bounds in lower-to-upper order. If the intended order is semantically meaningful, rename or restructure the rule instead of relying on the fix.

diagnostics.title: Consider adding [NotEmpty] for string property
diagnostics.summary: A string participates in validation but has no explicit empty-string decision. The analyzer suggests making that decision visible.
trigger: public string Name { get; set; } = string.Empty;
diagnostics.message: info VAL0011: Property "Name" is a string and participates in validation; consider adding [NotEmpty]
diagnostics.fix: Adds [NotEmpty] next to the existing string rule.
after: public string Name { get; set; } = string.Empty;
diagnostics.guidance: Add the attribute when the empty string is invalid. Keep the suggestion off when empty is a meaningful value, or configure the rule's message to explain that choice.

diagnostics.title: Consider adding [NotNull] for nullable property
diagnostics.summary: A nullable member has validation rules but no explicit null decision. The suggestion makes that decision visible.
diagnostics.message: info VAL0012: Property "Email" is nullable and has validation rules; consider adding [NotNull]
diagnostics.fix: Adds [NotNull] next to the nullable member's rule.
diagnostics.guidance: Add [NotNull] when null is invalid. Leave the member nullable and omit the attribute when null means the rule should be skipped.

diagnostics.title: Rule can be simplified
diagnostics.summary: Two comparison rules describe one range. A single range rule is shorter and keeps the lower and upper bounds together.
diagnostics.message: info VAL0013: The process of validating the property "Score" can be simplified by using "'InclusiveBetween' or 'ExclusiveBetween'" instead of "'GreaterThan' and 'LessThan'"
diagnostics.reason: Replacing two rules with one changes the documented rule set and may change inclusive/exclusive semantics; the author must choose the replacement.
diagnostics.guidance: For integer values greater than 0 and less than 10, use [InclusiveBetween(1, 9)] or [ExclusiveBetween(0, 10)] depending on the values the domain allows.

diagnostics.title: Redundant [NotNull] attribute
diagnostics.summary: [NotNull] is applied to a non-nullable value type, where it cannot change the result.
diagnostics.message: warning VAL0014: The property "Age" is non-nullable; [NotNull] is redundant and can be removed
diagnostics.fix: Removes the redundant [NotNull] while keeping sibling validation attributes.
diagnostics.guidance: Keep [NotNull] on nullable reference or value types where it expresses a real requirement. On a non-nullable value type it is noise.

diagnostics.title: Target property not found
diagnostics.summary: A property-comparison rule references a sibling member that does not exist on the model.
diagnostics.message: error VAL0015: Rule "PropertyEqual" references a property "Password" that does not exist on type "User"
diagnostics.reason: The intended sibling member name is user intent; the generator cannot know which member was meant.
diagnostics.guidance: Use nameof(Password) in fluent code, or correct the attribute string. The comparison target must be a readable member on the same model.

diagnostics.title: Synchronous Validate on async-only validator
diagnostics.summary: A validator marked [AsyncOnlyValidator] is called through the synchronous API, which would throw at runtime.
trigger: public void Check(IValidator<Order> validator, Order order)
diagnostics.message: warning VAL0016: "OrderService" is marked [AsyncOnlyValidator]; synchronous Validate() throws at runtime, use ValidateAsync() instead
diagnostics.fix: Rewrites the call to await ValidateAsync(...).
after: public async Task<ValidationResult> CheckAsync(IValidator<Order> validator, Order order) =>
diagnostics.guidance: Use the async path for async-only validators. If the call site must stay synchronous, add a synchronous rule to the validator instead of suppressing the warning.

diagnostics.title: Tautological validation rule
diagnostics.summary: The rule's bounds cover the full value range, so it can never fail. It adds cost without changing the result.
trigger: public string Name { get; set; } = string.Empty;
diagnostics.message: info VAL0017: The rule "MinimumLength" on member "Name" is always satisfied and can be removed
after: public string Name { get; set; } = string.Empty;
diagnostics.guidance: Keep the rule only when the explicit zero bound is useful documentation, and suppress the diagnostic locally with a reason in that case.

diagnostics.title: Invalid condition method
diagnostics.summary: A conditional attribute names a method that is missing or has an unsupported signature.
diagnostics.message: error VAL0018: Condition method "IsActive" on type "Order" must be an accessible instance or static method matching (Order instance) or (Order instance, ValidationContext<Order> context)
diagnostics.reason: The condition method must be authored or its signature chosen; the generator cannot provide business logic.
diagnostics.guidance: Add an accessible method returning bool with (T instance) or (T instance, ValidationContext<T> context). Instance and static methods are supported.

diagnostics.title: Invalid lifecycle hook
diagnostics.summary: A lifecycle attribute names a hook that is missing, non-static, or has the wrong return type or parameters.
diagnostics.message: error VAL0019: Lifecycle hook "BeforeValidate" on type "Order" must be a static method returning bool
diagnostics.reason: The hook must be authored or its signature chosen; the generator cannot invent lifecycle behavior.
diagnostics.guidance: Declare a static PreValidate method accepting (T, ValidationContext<T>) or (T, ValidationContext<T>, ValidationErrorCollector) and returning bool. OnFailure accepts ValidationResult and returns void.

diagnostics.title: Invalid custom validator
diagnostics.summary: A [CustomValidator] reference names a method that is missing or does not match a supported synchronous or asynchronous signature.
diagnostics.message: error VAL0020: Custom validator method "Validate" on type "OrderRules" must be a static method matching a supported signature
diagnostics.reason: The custom method must be authored or its signature chosen; the generator cannot guess the validation logic.
diagnostics.guidance: Use a static method returning bool or ValidationResult and accepting (TValue) or (TValue, IServiceProvider). Async methods set IsAsync = true, return ValueTask<bool> or ValueTask<ValidationResult>, and end with CancellationToken.

diagnostics.title: Invalid date/time rule value
diagnostics.summary: A date/time rule literal cannot be parsed as the member's date/time type under the invariant culture.
diagnostics.message: error VAL0021: The value "not-a-date" cannot be parsed as type "DateOnly" for the date/time rule on "StartsOn"
diagnostics.reason: The literal is unparseable; the intended date is unknown and the generator never substitutes DateTime.Now.
diagnostics.guidance: Use an invariant date/time literal for the member type, for example [After("2026-01-01")] on DateOnly. If the source is local time, normalize it at the boundary.

diagnostics.title: Model shape is not supported
diagnostics.summary: The source generator cannot emit a validator for this model shape. It fails closed instead of producing a partial or misleading validator.
diagnostics.message: error VAL0022: Type "Box<T>" cannot be validated by the source generator: generic models are not supported; use a non-generic model or a fluent validator
diagnostics.reason: The model shape must change or move to a fluent validator; a generator fix would have to choose a closed instantiation, namespace, or instance member.
diagnostics.guidance: Use a non-generic model with an explicit namespace and instance properties, or write a fluent validator for the unsupported shape. Global-namespace models and static validated properties report the same descriptor.

diagnostics.title: RuleFor member name mismatch
diagnostics.summary: The RuleFor expression selects one member but the string argument names another. The generated error path and client payload would be wrong.
diagnostics.message: warning VAL0023: RuleFor selects member "Name" but passes member name "Email"; use nameof(Customer.Name) or "Name"
diagnostics.fix: Rewrites the member-name argument to nameof(Model.Member).
diagnostics.guidance: Use nameof so the compiler keeps the expression and the reported member aligned. Custom paths and free-form names are intentionally not rewritten.

diagnostics.title: Collection rule requires a collection
diagnostics.summary: A cardinality rule such as Count, MinCount, or MaxCount is applied to a scalar member.
diagnostics.message: warning VAL0024: Rule "Count" requires a collection, but the target type is "int"
diagnostics.reason: The target member or the rule must change based on intent; the analyzer cannot know which one the author meant.
diagnostics.guidance: Apply cardinality rules to arrays or IEnumerable<T> members. Use [InclusiveBetween] for a numeric scalar or remove the cardinality rule.

diagnostics.title: Async-only validator in synchronous adapter
diagnostics.summary: A [JeninnetValidatable] adapter points at an async-only validator, but the DataAnnotations adapter calls the synchronous Validate API.
diagnostics.message: warning VAL0025: Validator "AsyncOrderValidator" is marked [AsyncOnlyValidator] but "Order" calls the synchronous DataAnnotations path; use an async integration path or add a synchronous rule
diagnostics.reason: The integration path or the validator must change based on intent; the adapter cannot silently switch to an async contract.
diagnostics.guidance: Use an async integration path, or add a synchronous rule to the validator so the DataAnnotations path can run it.

diagnostics.title: Sanitize cannot be applied
diagnostics.summary: Sanitization writes the cleaned value back in place, but the member has no writable setter or is not a supported sanitizable type.
trigger: public string Code { get; init; } = string.Empty;
diagnostics.message: error VAL0027: [Sanitize] cannot be applied to "Code": the member has an init-only setter
diagnostics.reason: Fixing the member setter or removing sanitization is a design decision; the generator cannot mutate an immutable member.
diagnostics.guidance: Give the member an accessible non-init setter, sanitize a writable copy, or remove the attribute. The fluent equivalent without a setter throws InvalidOperationException at configuration time.

diagnostics.title: SkipValidation conflicts with validation attributes
diagnostics.summary: [SkipValidation] drops every rule for the property, so the accompanying validation attributes never run.
diagnostics.message: warning VAL0028: [SkipValidation] on "Code" is combined with validation attributes; remove the attributes or the skip marker
diagnostics.reason: Removing the skip marker or removing the attributes depends on the author's intent; both are valid outcomes.
diagnostics.guidance: Keep [SkipValidation] and remove the validation attributes to opt out deliberately, or remove [SkipValidation] to let the rules run.

diagnostics.title: Conditional attribute has an invalid target
diagnostics.summary: A conditional attribute references a sibling member that does not exist, is static, or cannot be read by the generated validator.
diagnostics.message: error VAL0029: The conditional attribute "RequiredIf" on "Code" has an invalid target: no readable member "Missing" exists
diagnostics.reason: The intended sibling member is user intent; the generator cannot know which member the author meant.
diagnostics.guidance: Use nameof(...) with a readable instance member on the same model. Static members and self-references are rejected.

diagnostics.title: Conditional attribute value is not supported
diagnostics.summary: The conditional constant cannot be compared with the target member's type.
diagnostics.message: error VAL0030: The conditional attribute "RequiredIf" on "Reason" has an unsupported value: a Boolean member cannot be compared with "yes"
diagnostics.reason: The intended comparison value is user intent; the generator cannot choose between changing the value and changing the member type.
diagnostics.guidance: Match the constant to the sibling member's type: true for Boolean, a numeric literal for numeric types, and a parseable string for date/time, Guid, and TimeSpan members.

diagnostics.title: Conditional attribute is duplicated
diagnostics.summary: The same conditional attribute targets one member more than once, so the generated condition is ambiguous.
diagnostics.message: error VAL0031: The conditional attribute "RequiredIf" on "Reason" targets "IsActive" more than once; combine the conditions or remove the duplicate
diagnostics.reason: Which duplicate to keep is user intent; the generator cannot merge two different conditions safely.
diagnostics.guidance: Keep one condition per attribute type and target. Different conditional attribute types may target the same member; their conditions are combined with AND.

diagnostics.title: Relative date rule requires a date/time member
diagnostics.summary: [FutureDate] and [PastDate] compare a member with the current instant, so the member must have a date/time type.
diagnostics.message: error VAL0032: [FutureDate] on "When" requires DateTime, DateTimeOffset, or DateOnly; "string" is not supported
diagnostics.reason: The member type or the rule must change based on intent; TimeOnly has no date component and is not a substitute.
diagnostics.guidance: Use DateTime, DateTimeOffset, or DateOnly for the member, or use a custom/fluent rule for another representation.

diagnostics.title: Exclusive range has equal bounds
diagnostics.summary: An exclusive range with equal bounds can never match. The declaration describes an impossible validation.
diagnostics.message: error VAL0033: [ExclusiveBetween] on "Score" has equal bounds (5); an exclusive range can never match. Widen the bounds or use an inclusive range.
diagnostics.reason: Widening the bounds or switching to an inclusive range changes semantics; the author must choose the intended range.
diagnostics.guidance: Use a strict lower < upper range such as [ExclusiveBetween(4, 6)], or use [InclusiveBetween(5, 5)] when the single value is intended.

diagnostics.title: Invalid multiple-of divisor
diagnostics.summary: A multiple-of rule uses a divisor that is zero, negative, NaN, or infinite. The rule cannot produce a meaningful result.
diagnostics.message: error VAL0034: The divisor "0" for [MultipleOf] on "Amount" must be a positive finite number
diagnostics.reason: The intended positive divisor is user intent; the generator cannot choose a replacement divisor.
diagnostics.guidance: Use a positive finite divisor such as [MultipleOf(0.01)] for currency or [MultipleOf(5)] for a required increment.
